actions.action: Scratch test a few stems to check for green tissue
Prune stems that are brown and brittle back to healthy tissue
Once new growth is established, apply acid-loving plant fertilizer if needed
Water deeply during dry spells, about an inch per week
Replace gravel with a 2–3 inch layer of pine bark, pine straw, or shredded hardwood mulch kept away from stems

reason: The answer correctly calls it winter-reddened but living azaleas and advises deep watering, but it tells the owner to delay the fertilizing that helped, so the advice only partly matches; nothing in it is likely to hurt the plant.
